title: Engineering a Quantum Thermal Diode with Floquet Driving
authors: Aqsa Rehman, M. Tahir Naseem, Adam Zaman Chaudhry
abstract: Controlling heat flow in small quantum systems is a central goal of quantum thermodynamics and nanoscale transport. A key challenge is to achieve strong thermal rectification without suppressing the transmitted heat current, a tradeoff that often arises in static diode configurations. We establish a Floquet-control mechanism in a minimal quantum thermal diode formed by two longitudinally modulated Ising-coupled qubits, each coupled to an independent thermal reservoir. From a microscopic system--bath model, we derive a Floquet--LGKS master equation that resolves the drive-assisted transition channels. The resonant undriven device with left--right symmetric bath couplings serves as the reciprocal benchmark, while static detuning provides a rectifying reference with reduced heat current. Single-side driving breaks this reciprocal structure by creating a Floquet-dressed contact opposite a purely thermal contact. For this configuration, we obtain a compact steady-state current formula and an exact blocking condition for suppressing one bias direction while retaining finite transport in the opposite direction. In the weak sinusoidal-drive regime, rectification begins quadratically in the modulation amplitude. Dual-side driving adds a Floquet pumping contribution to the interaction-mediated current, so complete blocking requires cancellation of both contributions. These results establish contact-selective Floquet dressing as a design principle for controllable heat-flow asymmetry in minimal quantum thermal devices.
summary: The paper demonstrates how applying periodic external fields (Floquet driving) to a coupled qubit system can engineer a quantum thermal diode. By breaking the symmetry of coupling—specifically through single-side modulation—the authors achieve strong, controllable heat rectification. This establishes contact-selective Floquet dressing as a powerful design tool for managing energy flow in nanoscale quantum devices.
main_problem: The central goal is controlling heat flow at the nanoscale by achieving strong thermal rectification without sacrificing the overall transmitted heat current, a known trade-off in static quantum diodes.
main_result: Contact-selective Floquet dressing provides a robust design principle to engineer controllable and tunable asymmetry in heat flow through minimal quantum thermal devices.
method: The analysis involves deriving and solving a Floquet–LGKS master equation from a microscopic system--bath model, comparing driven dynamics against static and undriven benchmarks.
model_or_system: The system is a minimal quantum thermal diode composed of two longitudinally modulated Ising-coupled qubits, each coupled independently to its own thermal reservoir. The dynamics are governed by time-dependent Hamiltonians and resolved via Floquet theory.
key_observables: Steady-state heat current ($J_{ss}$), thermal rectification coefficient ($R$), and the blocking condition (suppressing one bias direction while maintaining transport in the other).
important_parameters: The modulation amplitude ($\alpha$) is crucial, as rectification scales quadratically with it in the weak-drive regime; single-side vs. dual-side driving configurations are key parameters.
main_assumptions: The system–bath coupling is assumed to be weak, and approximations like Born, Markov, and Floquet–secular methods are employed for solving the master equation.
figures_summary: Figure 1 schematically illustrates the setup: two qubits with modulated frequencies coupled by an Ising interaction, connected to independent thermal reservoirs ($T_L, T_R$).
paper_structure: The paper establishes the physical model and Hamiltonian; it derives the Floquet-LGKS master equation; it analyzes single-side driving to achieve rectification and blocking; finally, it extends the analysis to dual-side driving, showing how pumping contributions must cancel for complete blockade.
why_interesting: This work directly addresses non-equilibrium quantum thermodynamics by using time-periodic driving (Floquet engineering) to manipulate energy flow directionality in mesoscopic systems, which is highly relevant to open quantum system dynamics and thermal management.
